title: Residential Property and Owners' Association Disclosure Statement
description: North Carolina requires sellers of residential real property (1-4 dwelling units) to complete and deliver the Residential Property and Owners' Association Disclosure Statement to the buyer. The form covers structural, mechanical, environmental, and other known conditions. Seller must answer all questions or indicate 'No Representation.' Must be delivered before the buyer makes an offer.

required_actions.note: Must be delivered before buyer makes an offer. Buyer may rescind within 3 days of receipt if not provided timely.

title: Working With Real Estate Agents Disclosure
description: North Carolina requires brokers to provide the 'Working With Real Estate Agents' brochure at first substantial contact with a prospective buyer or seller. The brochure explains the types of agency available in NC: seller's agent, buyer's agent, and dual agent. Designated dual agency is permitted with written consent.

title: Mineral and Oil/Gas Rights Disclosure
description: North Carolina requires disclosure when mineral, oil, or gas rights have been severed from the surface estate. The seller must disclose whether any subsurface mineral rights have been previously conveyed or reserved by prior owners. This is particularly relevant in western NC mining areas and Piedmont regions.

required_actions.note: Mineral rights disclosure included on NC-RPOADS. Must identify any severed mineral interests.
Buyer should conduct independent mineral rights title search in areas with known mining history.

citations: NCGS §113A-234 (Energy Exploration, Development, and Production Act)

title: Closing Type — Attorney Required
description: North Carolina is an attorney-closing state. The NC State Bar has determined that real estate closings constitute the practice of law and must be conducted under the supervision of a licensed North Carolina attorney. The closing attorney reviews all documents, conducts the title examination, and certifies the title.

required_actions.note: Licensed NC attorney must supervise closing. Title examination and certification by attorney required.

citations: NC State Bar 2002 Formal Ethics Op. 1

title: Synthetic Stucco (EIFS) Disclosure
description: North Carolina requires specific disclosure if the property has synthetic stucco (Exterior Insulation and Finish System or EIFS). The seller must disclose the presence of EIFS and any known moisture intrusion issues. EIFS-related moisture damage has been a significant issue in NC real estate.

required_actions.note: EIFS/synthetic stucco disclosure on NC-RPOADS. Include any moisture intrusion test results.

citations: NC Building Code — EIFS inspection requirements
